{{Quote|The illness has returned, my children. Let us cure it.|Final Prophet Ber'asco|<ref name="Otherspace" />}}
The [[Starship/Legends|starship]] ''[[Desolate]]'', in the dimension known as [[Otherspace]], was the site of a '''skirmish''' during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], at some point between [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] and [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]]. Following a [[Mutiny on the Celestial|mutiny]] on the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Prison ship/Legends|prison ship]] ''[[Celestial (starship)|Celestial]]'', the damaged [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]] of both the ''Celestial'' and the Rebel [[GX1 short hauler/Legends|ship]] ''[[Long Shot]]'' deposited them in Otherspace.

While the crews of the two ships investigated the nearby ''Desolate'', they encountered the [[Alien/Legends|alien]] vessel's inhabitants: the [[Charon/Legends|Charon]]. Most of the mutineers were [[Death/Legends|killed]] or captured, including their ringleaders: [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Ravik/Legends|Ravik]] and [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Bane Nothos]]. The crew of the ''Long Shot'', meanwhile, battled Charon [[Warrior (Charon)|warriors]] as they located various replacement parts for their broken [[Hyperdrive motivator/Legends|hyperdrive motivator]].

Ravik ultimately allied with the Charon [[Final Prophet]] [[Ber'asco]], and the two beseeched the Rebels to aid Ber'asco in returning to the [[The galaxy/Legends|known galaxy]] and wiping out all of its life, in accordance with the beliefs of the [[Charon Death Cult]]. The Rebels refused and mounted an escape, ultimately fleeing Otherspace with a repaired hyperdrive. The undaunted Charon continued on their crusade, [[Bioengineering/Legends|merging]] Ravik with a [[Biocomputer/Legends|biocomputer]] and using his knowledge to build a hyperdrive of their own. Their next step was a [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] invasion.
 
==Prelude==
{{Dialogue|Mott|She's dead, Moff. ''Celestial'' has had it. We couldn't build a solid system boat out of what's left.|Ravik|Nothos, what have you got on that asteroid or planetoid… whatever… out there.|Nothos|"Grand Moff, I believe the object out there is a ship.|attr=Celis Mott, Grand Moff Ravik, and Bane Nothos discover the ''Desolate'' in Otherspace|src=<ref name="Otherspace" />}}
At some point between [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]<ref name="Date note 1" /> and [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]],<ref name="Date note 2" /> during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], [[Prisoner/Legends|inmates]] aboard the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Prison ship/Legends|prison ship]] ''[[Celestial (starship)|Celestial]]'' [[Mutiny on the Celestial|took control]] of the [[Starship/Legends|vessel]]. Its [[Captain/Legends|captain]], [[Alain Gryphon]], desperately sent the ship into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] before reinforcements from the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] could arrive, but the ship's [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] had been damaged during the insurrection. As such, the ''Celestial'' ended up in the mysterious dimension known as [[Otherspace]].<ref name="Otherspace" />
 
Although several crewmembers of the ''Celestial'' had allied with them, the escaped [[Prison/Legends|prisoners]] found themselves masters of a dying ship. Imperial [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Bane Nothos]] was convinced he could command the starship ''[[Desolate]]'', an amorphous mass floating in nearby space, and so he and his fellows brought the captive ''Celestial''{{'s}} crew over in [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]]. Another Rebel [[GX1 short hauler/Legends|ship]], the ''[[Long Shot]]'', arrived in Otherspace shortly afterward via a faulty hyperdrive of its own following a [[Space warfare/Legends|fight]] with the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] ''[[Relentless (Dorja)|Relentless]]''.<ref name="Otherspace" />
 
==The skirmish==
{{Quote|The disease rarely has vectored to ''Desolate'', never before within The Nest. Your strain is most resistant. Ravik-culture has convinced me of your value in service to the Void. I am the Final Prophet of the Charon. I am Ber'asco. Submit to the will of Void; bioscientists can evaluate, cultivate your strain. Agree to construction; we shall cross you with finest of Charon warriors. You accept our offer?|Ber'asco, to the ''Long Shot''{{'s}} crew|<ref name="Otherspace" />}}
[[File:Longshotentersdesolate.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The ''Long Shot'' enters the ''Desolate''.]]
Aboard the ''Desolate'' were the [[Charon Death Cult]], who believed that all life must return to the [[Void of Death]]. [[Ber'asco]], the [[Prophet of the Void]], was awoken by a [[Charon/Legends|Charon]] [[bioscientist]] when the escape pods arrived, and he was told that a disease had invaded their vessel. He commanded that Charon [[Warrior (Charon)|warriors]] be roused from [[death-sleep]], and that [[death mist]] be prepared to fight the invading disease. Those [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] investigated the ''Celestial'' to learn about their enemy's metabolism and biodefenses before returning to the ''Desolate''.<ref name="Otherspace" />
 
Warriors also met the escape pods' occupants as soon as they boarded the ''Desolate'', overwhelming them in the darkness with bites and [[Charon venom|poison]]-tipped claws. Most of the group was captured or [[Death/Legends|killed]], including the Rebel [[Conners]], who was dragged away. The insurrectionists&mdash;led by Nothos and [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Ravik/Legends|Ravik]]&mdash;ran off, leaving the Alliance crew to fend for themselves; Captain Gryphon was [[Poison/Legends|poisoned]] and left to die. Meanwhile, the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] who had aided in the takeover quickly abandoned their Imperial comrades and struck off on their own.<ref name="Otherspace" />
 
Meanwhile, the ''Long Shot''{{'s}} crew explored the ''Celestial'' themselves, in search of a new [[Hyperdrive motivator/Legends|hyperdrive motivator]], before taking their hunt to the ''Desolate''. They made their way across a graveyard of derelict ships before entering their target through a membrane, disembarking on the first and bottom of four platforms within. Inside the ship's [[growing chamber]], they found a dying Captain Gryphon, who warned them of what lay ahead before succumbing to the poison.<ref name="Otherspace" />

[[File:Exploringthedesolate.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Rebels explore the alien vessel.]]
The Rebels' next stop was an overlook on the first level. The [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Celis Mott]], one of the escaped prisoners, awaited them, along with three mutinous crewmembers of the ''Celestial''. Red death mist had turned them mad, and they were claiming the overlook as their own territory. After that encounter, the Rebels found a [[hypercoil]] in a cargo hold and were forced to fight off red mist themselves, before taking a crawltube up to the second level. A [[power coupler]] was located in the [[Hangar/Legends|hangar bay]], followed by a collection of impenetrable [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Computer/Legends|computers]], and a Charon warrior attacked them when they reached the [[chamber of armor]].<ref name="Otherspace" />

Although decked in [[Charon battle armor|battle armor]], the Charon warrior was bested, and the Rebels continued on into the [[chamber of nutrients]]. There, they were confronted by [[floating glob]]s, which functioned as the ship's waste removal units. In the next room, [[Hologram/Legends|holograms]] taught the explorers about the Charon's history, and in a common area, they ran into Bane Nothos. They were forced to battle four more Charon warriors during this melee, and finally, they reached platform three. There, captured crewmembers of the nearby derelict ships were stored in pods as [[Fuel/Legends|fuel]] for the ship's [[Power core/Legends|power core]]. Their [[Brain/Legends|brains]] were nearly destroyed, and the Rebels could not rescue them.<ref name="Otherspace" />

Near the pods was another piece of hypderdrive technology: a [[4-axial stabilizer]]. Next on the strange journey was the [[Hall of Contests]], a place for Charon [[Scientist/Legends|bioscientists]] to pit living specimens against their own [[Bioengineering/Legends|bio-engineered]] constructs. While the Rebels battled constructs such as [[shootcrawler]]s, [[Jumper (Charon)|jumpers]], the [[gatebeast]], and the [[Weaver (Charon)|weaver]], the [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] [[EL-434]] escaped from three entangling webs and joined the fray; the bounty hunter [[Zardra]] also arrived on the scene. The next encounter was with bioscientists in the [[Laboratory/Legends|construct chamber]], where the Rebels also found an [[influx capacitor]]. In the [[chamber of sleep]], 200 warriors were awakening from their death-[[Sleep/Legends|sleep]].<ref name="Otherspace" />

[[File:Fightberasco.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Encountering Ber'asco, the Final Prophet]]
Only five warriors were immediately ready for battle, however. After defeating them, the explorers ascended to level four and blocked the crawltube behind them. Passing the ship's power core, they entered a room known as the [[altar of death]]. Not only did a giant monolith in the center zap some of their life forces away, but a Charon construct called the [[Cathorn]] also appeared to challenge them. Subsequent passage through another computer room brought them to their final destination: the ''Desolate''{{'s}} command [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], known as the nest. There, they found the final piece they needed for their hyperdrive motivator: a [[realspace compensator]].<ref name="Otherspace" />

Also in the nest were the last of the ''Celestial''{{'s}} crew, tangled in a web, their minds destroyed by venom. Charon warriors were there, too, awaiting the explorers, and accompanied by an honored guest: Grand Moff Ravik. He had negotiated his survival by gifting the ''Celestial''{{'s}} crewmembers to the [[Prophet/Legends|prophet]] Ber'asco, and by offering to lead the Charon on a crusade into his own [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="Otherspace" />

Ravik hoped the ''Long Shot''{{'s}} crew would join him&mdash;if the Rebel Alliance worked with and acted as a balance against the Charon while they destroyed the Empire, he believed he could emerge as the new [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]]. Ravik thought the prospect of dethroning [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] would convince the Rebels to agree. Their decision proved immaterial, though, as Ber'asco, the [[Final Prophet]], emerged and insisted on genetically crossing them with Charon warriors either way.<ref name="Otherspace" />

When the Rebels refused to submit to Charon bioscientists, Ber'asco activated the nest's defenses: six tendrils attacked, each one capped with a glowing sphere that fired [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]] bolts. While the Rebels fought for their lives, Ber'asco and his warriors evacuated and opened the room's domed ceiling to the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of space. The explorers only managed to escape by hurrying into unwieldy Charon [[Environment suit/Legends|environment suits]], and a harrowing 100-[[Meter/Legends|meter]] walk across the surface of the ''Desolate'' ensued.<ref name="Otherspace" />

[[File:Escapethedesolate.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The ''Long Shot'' escapes.]]
Vac-suited Charon followed them across the [[Hull/Legends|hull]], and when they reached the entry portal where the ''Long Shot'' was parked, they found it covered in webbing. With Zardra's help, they also finished off four more Charon warriors. Fleeing from dozens more, they boarded their ship and took off at [[Sublight engine/Legends|sublight]] speed while they repaired their hyperdrive. Charon [[bio-fighter]]s [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dueled]] them, but the Rebels were ultimately able to jump to [[Lightspeed/Legends|lightspeed]].<ref name="Otherspace" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|The others of your strain have fled, running to hide in a place we cannot yet reach. The Void is disappointed. Ravik&ndash;culture is all we have left. We are taking utmost precautions in constructing you. When you are free of the disease you shall lead us to your strain. The Void is patient. Soon its patience shall be rewarded.|Ber'asco, to Ravik, following the Rebels' escape|<ref name="Otherspace" />}}
After learning that other dimensions existed and were full of the evil that was life, the Charon vowed to complete their holy mission by rendering every dimension completely desolate. They integrated Ravik into their [[Biocomputer/Legends|biological computer]], using his thoughts and knowledge to build their own hyperdrive; Ravik, however, was able to resist the complete destruction of his personality, and he bided his [[Time/Legends|time]] for [[Standard month/Legends|months]] until the hyperdrive was ready.<ref name="Otherspace II: Invasion" />

When Ber'asco mind-linked with the biocomputer to get jump coordinates, Ravik bested him in a mental duel, and he took control of Ber'asco's body. He then led the Charon into the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] in an invasion that culminated with the [[Battle of Stronghold]]. Ber'asco, meanwhile, transferred his mind into Bane Nothos, whom the Charon had captured and placed into [[Suspended animation/Legends|cryogenic sleep]]. In his new body, he hunted Ravik down.<ref name="Otherspace II: Invasion" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|What if the PCs join Ber'asco? The first step is to be injected with Charon poison; if the PCs go that far the adventure is over. Ber'asco has won. Let the PCs know that they become NPCs if they become constructs, as they lose their free will.|Instructions to the [[Wikipedia:Gamemaster|gamemaster]] of ''Otherspace'', near the end of the adventure|<ref name="Otherspace" />}}
The skirmish on the ''Desolate'' forms the bulk of the adventure book ''[[Otherspace (adventure)|Otherspace]]'', published by [[West End Games]] in [[1989]]. It was written by [[Bill Slavicsek]], and various illustrations of the skirmish were drawn by artist [[Jeff Dee]]. The player characters of the adventure's campaign are the Rebel crew of the ''Long Shot'', and although the order of events in their journey through the ''Desolate'' remains constant, each event can play out in many different ways based on player choices and rolls of the dice.<ref name="Otherspace" />

This article endeavors to give only vague outlines of each event in their mission and to avoid speculating on details of how individual encounters with [[Wikipedia:Non-player character|NPCs]] [[Star Wars Legends|canonically]] play out&mdash;however, it assumes that the mission is a success, as the follow-up adventure ''[[Otherspace II: Invasion]]'' confirms in its opening pages that the Rebels rebuilt their hyperdrive and escaped back into realspace.<ref name="Otherspace II: Invasion" />
